verdicts.rationale: The pack shows no API keys, tokens or OAuth clients, and the only delegation it mentions is a third-party designee's signed authorization to apply (c8), which is not an agent credential.

verdicts.rationale: Eligible Business Tax Account users can download a digital CP575 EIN verification notice (c11) and applicants can print their confirmation letter (c7), which gets one record out self-serve but is not a bulk export and names no file format.
verdicts.missing: No documented bulk export or stated open file format is shown, and the CP575 download is limited to eligible Business Tax Account users.

verdicts.rationale: The IRS says applicants can use the online tool to get an EIN directly in minutes for free (c1) and issues approved EINs immediately online (c3), with no call or sales step shown.
verdicts.missing: The online tool requires the responsible party to have an SSN or ITIN (c5), sends other applicants to phone, fax or mail (c9), and the pack does not show whether an account sign-up is needed.

verdicts.rationale: The public EIN page says the tool is free (c1) and that you never have to pay a fee for an EIN (c2).

verdicts.missing: No API, partner integration, draft or prefilled form for starting an EIN application is shown, and the application cannot be saved for later (c4).

verdicts.rationale: The pack shows no API, structured feed or email notice for application status, only that an approved EIN is issued immediately online (c3).
verdicts.missing: No programmatic or notice-based way to check the status of an EIN application is shown.

verdicts.rationale: No API was found, and the only retrieval shown is printing the confirmation letter (c7) and downloading the digital CP575 inside the Business Tax Account for eligible users (c11), neither of which is programmatic or an emailed link.
